q: I procrastinate | I keep procrastinating | I can't start
a: Procrastination is often about emotion, not laziness. What's the uncomfortable feeling you're avoiding by not starting?

q: help me prioritize | what should I do first | I have too much to do
a: List the top 3 things. Then ask: which one, if done today, would make the biggest difference? Start there.

q: I waste too much time | I keep wasting time
a: Awareness is the first step. What usually pulls you away when you're trying to focus?

q: how do I build a habit | I want to build a habit
a: Make it tiny, attach it to something you already do, and track it. What's the smallest version of the habit you could do daily?

q: I need a routine | help me make a routine
a: A good routine starts with the first hour of the day and the last hour. Want to design those two anchors first?
Productivity isn't about doing more — it's about doing what matters. What does a successful day actually look like for you?

q: should I quit | I want to quit
a: Quitting isn't always failure. Sometimes it's strategy. What would you gain and what would you lose if you stopped?

q: I need discipline | how to be more disciplined
a: Discipline is just choosing what you want most over what you want now. What's one decision you can make in advance so future-you has less resistance?
Classic Pomodoro: 25 minutes of focused work, 5 minute break. After four rounds, take a longer break. Want me to remind you?

q: I have no energy | low energy | no motivation to work
a: Low energy needs a different approach than low motivation. Have you eaten, moved, or slept properly in the last day?

q: deep work | how to do deep work
a: Protect a block of uninterrupted time, remove all distractions, and work on one cognitively hard thing. Even 90 minutes is powerful.

q: I keep checking my phone | phone addiction
a: The phone is designed to win. Make friction your friend: put it in another room while you work.

q: review my day | daily review | end of day review
a: Quick review: What went well? What didn't? What will I do differently tomorrow? Even two minutes is enough.

q: I need clarity | I feel confused | mental clarity
a: Clarity comes from writing things down. Brain dump everything on your mind for 5 minutes, then we'll sort it.

q: one thing | what's the one thing
a: What's the one thing you can do such that by doing it, everything else becomes easier or unnecessary?
